title: Manifest
description: One file's worth of schema — serves both root manifests and included modules; the resolver enforces which fields are legal in which role.

includes.description: Root manifests only. Local `./path` sources in Phase A.

name.description: Display name shown in the guided flow header; defaults to the directory name.

registries.description: Reserved for Phase C — rejected with a clear message if present.

steps.description: Named, reusable script fragments (referenced via `use:` in run lists).

vars.description: Modules only: variables the include site binds.

version.description: Checked via `VersionProbe` before full parsing; kept so the schema is complete and future versions can branch on it.

category.description: Display grouping for the guided flow, the palette, and `--list`: an author-assigned label ("Deploy", "Tests"). Commands sharing a category are grouped together regardless of which file declared them — a module tagging its exports "Deploy" joins the local "Deploy" group. When unset, grouping falls back to the include origin (see `ResolvedCommand::group_label`), so a manifest with no categories at all degrades to today's flat list/menu.

check.description: Optional readiness probe: a shell command (no `{param}` placeholders — it runs before params exist) whose exit 0 means "ready to run". Surfaced by `pult doctor` and by UIs before the run button; never run implicitly before `run:` — preflight steps in the playbook remain the mitigation.

description.description: One or two sentences explaining what the command does, shown by `--help`, `--list --json`, and UIs — the title names the control, the description explains it.

interactive.description: Declares that `run:` requires a controlling terminal at runtime (REPLs, TUIs, shells into containers). The contract: an *undeclared* command must be fully non-interactive once its params are filled — declare a param, don't `read` — which is what makes non-terminal surfaces safe. The plain CLI ignores it (stdio is inherited either way).

DynamicInputsDef.description: A parameter *set* discovered at run time: `from:`'s stdout lines become `key=value` pairs (parsed the same as `pick.from`, via `parse_dynamic_line`), each becoming its own runtime param under a key the manifest never names — the author declares only that the set exists, not which keys it has. Nothing consumes this yet; the resolver and executor wire it up in a later change.

from.description: Shell command whose stdout lines become the discovered keys. May interpolate `{param}` for params declared *earlier* in the same command — the resolver's dependent-ordering check covers this field too, the same rule `pick.from` follows.

secret.description: Whether every discovered value is a credential: masked wherever an interpolated command line is displayed, prompted without echo, and journaled as `<redacted>`. Defaults to **`true`** — the opposite of `input.secret`'s default. An `input:` author declares one known value and can judge whether it's a secret; a `dynamic-inputs` author cannot enumerate what discovery may someday return, so fail-safe is the only defensible default: forgetting `secret: false` costs an over-redacted-but-harmless journal, while forgetting `secret: true` would echo credentials into scrollback and a durable journal. Do not "fix" this asymmetry with `input:`'s default — it's deliberate.

description.description: Shown as `value — description` in the picker; display-only.

outputs.description: Shell variable names this step promises to set.

secret.description: Secret values are prompted without echo and masked wherever an interpolated command line is displayed (`running:` banner, `--print`, the ephemeral trust prompt). A `default:` is rejected for secrets — a default would be a credential committed to the manifest.

OptionDef.description:
A pick option: a plain value, or a value with a display description.

Deliberately *not* `#[serde(untagged)]` — see the manual `Deserialize` below for why. The `JsonSchema` derive can't read a `#[serde(untagged)]` attribute off a manually-`Deserialize`d type, so it gets schemars' own untagged marker (test-only) to keep the emitted schema "string-or-mapping", matching the `StepDef` idiom.

ParamDef.description: A param is a picker, free input, a reference to a named param, or a runtime-discovered set; exactly one of the four must be set (validated at load, so `kind()` is infallible).

dynamic-inputs.description: `dynamic-inputs` is the manifest's first hyphenated field — future multiword fields follow the same precedent. schemars honors the rename (proven already by `use_` above), so the committed schema emits the hyphenated key, not `dynamic_inputs`.

from.description: Shell command whose stdout lines become the options. May interpolate `{param}` for params declared *earlier* in the same command.

PipeUseRef.description: A step in a pipe contributes stdout only, so no `exports:` here.

RunSpec.description: `run:` is a single command line (executed via `sh -c`, exactly the original behavior) or a step list compiled into one bash script (see compile.rs).

StepDef.description: A step: a plain script string, or a script with a declared contract.

exports.description: Rename the step's declared outputs: `{ TASK: BACKEND_TASK }`.

with.description: Rebind the step's `{placeholder}` names (values may reference this command's params).
